audited_preprint.author: Preda Mihailescu
audited_preprint.claimed_result: no solutions to (x^p+y^p)/(x+y)=p^e z^q for distinct odd primes p>3 and q
audited_preprint.title: The strong Fermat-Catalan Equation

conditional_repeated_exponent_sieve.closed_subfamily: if gcd(p-1,q-1)=2 and q>3, no solution can satisfy the imported splitting hypothesis
conditional_repeated_exponent_sieve.gcd_form: with g=gcd(p-1,q-1), ord_q(2) divides g and therefore q divides 2^g-1
conditional_repeated_exponent_sieve.imported_hypothesis: the preprint arguments before the invalid fixed-field inference correctly prove D_2 intersect H_prime is trivial for a hypothetical solution

correct_group_theorem.equivalence: D_r intersect H_prime is trivial iff ord_q(r) divides ord_p(r)
correct_group_theorem.proof: powers with trivial G_prime coordinate are the multiples of m=ord_p(r); the intersection is trivial exactly when the H_prime coordinate also has b^m=1, i.e. n divides m

group_setup.decomposition_group: D_r=< (Frob_r mod p, Frob_r mod q) >
group_setup.unramified_rational_prime: r distinct from p and q

impact.global_limit: the sieve is not contractive in p and does not eliminate all repeated-prime signatures
impact.next_target: independently certify the preprint ideal-splitting lemma or replace it with a modular proof, then combine the order sieve with existing (p,p,q) asymptotic results
impact.valid_advance: the claimed universal theorem is withdrawn, but its splitting input would still yield an explicit Mersenne-divisor sieve on the repeated-prime exponent pairs

invalid_inference.claimed_conclusion: L^(D_r) contains Q(zeta_q), equivalently D_r is contained in G_prime
invalid_inference.reason: trivial intersection with a direct-product factor does not force trivial projection to that factor

nonclaim: This audit does not prove the strong Fermat-Catalan theorem, the repeated-prime Beal core, or Beal. The Mersenne-divisor condition is conditional on the preprint's earlier ideal-splitting argument, which has not been independently certified.

conditions: p and q distinct odd primes
